title: Dedicated throughput entitlement: measurement method, breach remediation, and contract language
creator: Sofia Green
description:
Purpose: Draft a precise, auditable definition of dedicated throughput entitlements for contract language, including how committed throughput is measured, how breaches are detected, the error budget accounting model, and the remediation/crediting process. This ticket consolidates PM position, engineering measurement requirements, legal fallback language, and ops runbook hooks.

Scope:
- Define the canonical metric (committed throughput units, measurement windows, and percentile used).
- Specify the error budget model for capacity shortfalls and the credit formula.
- Create contract clauses for notice periods, remediation windows, and customer remedies.
- Align autoscaling and burst policy behavior with SLA guarantees (what counts as a breach vs. expected autoscale behavior).
- Identify required telemetry and dashboards for customer-facing reporting and internal verification.

Out of scope: pricing negotiation for individual customers and bespoke SLAs for enterprise deals (those will be separate contract addenda).
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical metric is defined and documented (examples: committed RPS, committed token-rate, and mapping to model shards) and agreed by Eng and PM.
Measurement window and percentile are specified (e.g., rolling 7-day window, 99th percentile, or agreed alternative) and instrumentation requirements are listed.
Error budget accounting model is specified with worked examples showing how credits are computed for a sample outage pattern.
Contract language (2 variants: concise SLA clause for standard TOS, and expanded clause for enterprise SOW) is drafted and accepted by Legal as a starting template.
Autoscale and burst behavior is explicitly documented: which events trigger breach calculations, how burst credits are applied, and tie-in to dedicated fleet controls.
A verification plan exists: dashboards and reports that the customer and Redwood can use to reconcile reported breaches (links to dashboards and the query definitions).
updates: 2026-02-20 SG: Ticket created with initial problem statement and scope. Proposed canonical metric: committed tokens/sec per customer allocation. Asked Eng for feasibility analysis.

2026-03-06 ML: Autoscale integration spike complete. Confirmed that transient autoscale events < 5 minutes will be classified as non-breach if burst capacity covered the shortfall. Need explicit definition in contract.

2026-03-10 SG: Walkthrough with Billing — clarified crediting format (proportional credit expressed as percentage of monthly committed fee, with a minimum $X administrative credit). Billing asked for an escrow example; created worked example in acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12 LK (Legal): Reviewed clause variants; requested removal of absolute cure requirements and addition of force majeure and maintenance windows language. Legal asked for standard 30-day cure notice before termination rights are allowed.

Priya Nair (Billing) — 2026-02-28: Billing prefers a credit formula that is deterministic and easy to compute on invoices; suggested 'credit = committed_fee * (aggregated_shortfall_seconds / measurement_window_seconds) * severity_factor'.
Liam O'Connor (Support) — 2026-03-04: We need a playbook for customer-facing communications when a breach is detected; recommend a 'notice -> investigation -> provisional credit' flow.

2026-03-06: Autoscale policy — short bursts handled by burst pool do not count as breaches if latency remains below latency SLO and the burst duration < 300s. This will be encoded into the breach detection query.
2026-03-12: Legal feedback accepted — add 30-day cure notice and maintenance exclusion clause; update drafts and re-circulate to stakeholders.
